hypotheses.statement: The settlement failure ratio increased to 0.61 due to two concurrent, independent faults: database connection pool exhaustion caused by a worker concurrency increase without a corresponding pool size increase, and feature-flag service token expiry causing 401 errors.
The first remediation (increasing the database connection pool size to 64 at 17:20:15Z) resolved the pool exhaustion errors, reducing the failure ratio from 0.61 to 0.29.
The second remediation (installing a replacement token for flags.internal at 18:12:10Z) resolved the 401 errors, reducing the failure ratio from 0.29 to 0.004.

observed_facts.statement: An alert for settlement failure ratio above objective fired at 16:00:44Z and cleared at 18:12:30Z.
A configuration change at 15:55:00Z raised settlement-worker concurrency from 8 to 32 workers, while the database connection pool size remained at 20.
The service token for flags.internal expired at 15:59:00Z on 2026-02-11, and its renewal was not automated.

From 15:58:10Z, settlement-worker experienced database connection pool exhaustion (pool size 20, checked-out 20, queue depth rising) with pool_timeout errors after 5000ms, affecting approximately 0.38 of attempts.
From 15:59:02Z, settlement-worker calls to flags.internal returned 401 invalid_token, affecting approximately 0.31 of attempts, overlapping with pool_timeout failures on some attempts.
At 17:20:15Z, the connection pool was raised to 64, pool_timeout errors stopped, and the settlement failure ratio fell from 0.61 to 0.29.
At 18:12:10Z, a replacement token for flags.internal was installed, 401 responses stopped, and the settlement failure ratio fell from 0.29 to 0.004.
INC-2201 was opened at 16:05:00Z with severity 1, title 'Settlements failing', and recorded no settlement value at risk.

open_questions.missing_evidence: Documentation or configuration management records explaining the design decision.
open_questions.question: Why is the database connection pool size not derived from the worker concurrency?

open_questions.missing_evidence: An audit report or inventory of service tokens and their renewal configurations.
open_questions.question: Which other service tokens are on manual renewal and may be at risk of similar expiry?

summary: Incident dual-cause-payments involved a dual-fault scenario: a database connection pool exhaustion due to a worker concurrency increase without pool adjustment, and an expired feature-flag service token. These independent issues caused a settlement failure ratio spike to 0.61. Remediation occurred in two steps: first enlarging the pool (reducing failures to 0.29), then replacing the token (resolving to 0.004).

timeline.statement: Configuration change raised settlement-worker concurrency from 8 to 32 workers; database connection pool size remained at 20.
settlement-worker database connection pool exhausted (pool size 20, checked-out 20), causing pool_timeout errors affecting ~0.38 of attempts.
The service token for flags.internal expired; its renewal was not automated.
settlement-worker calls to flags.internal began returning 401 invalid_token, affecting ~0.31 of attempts, overlapping with pool_timeout failures.
Alert 'settlement failure ratio above objective' fired as settlement failure ratio reached 0.61 against an objective of 0.02.
INC-2201 opened with severity 1, title 'Settlements failing'.
Connection pool raised to 64; pool_timeout errors stopped and settlement failure ratio fell from 0.61 to 0.29.
Replacement token for flags.internal installed; 401 responses stopped and settlement failure ratio fell from 0.29 to 0.004.
Alert 'settlement failure ratio above objective' cleared.
